issue.title: drift(pin-mismatch): DRIFT_TRIANGLE.md pinned sha256 traces to the divergent rapp-god mirror, not canonical kody-w/RAPP; four-leg model predates RAPP1's quarantine of rapp-map's copy
issue.body:
## drift(pin-mismatch) — MEDIUM

**Filed by:** weekly Article LIII standing-guard sweep (2026-07-20), checking the RAPP-Bible DRIFT_TRIANGLE.md pin per `kody-w/RAPP` CONSTITUTION Article LIII.

**Exact surface:** `DRIFT_TRIANGLE.md` (live, main)

**Finding — two related problems:**

1. **Pin traces to the wrong leg.** Line 3 and the check-3 pin (`This Bible renders v1.2.0, sha256 f1ddcf7e1302a82195fa682ad94140d0d066bbe60647befc5030ec5b50507e9e`) match `kody-w/rapp-god/api/v1/ecosystem-spec.json`'s current bytes — but that file is itself byte-divergent from the canonical source (see companion issue kody-w/rapp-god#9, filed same sweep). The canonical `kody-w/RAPP/specs/ecosystem-spec.json` — the JSON's own self-declared `"canonical_source": "kody-w/RAPP"`, and `RAPP1_OWNER_ACTIONS.md`'s designated "Canonical ecosystem source" — has sha256 `0eb8146b62af8e8473d2ca8944ed8aff69e18e41a143eb1ef466f3c3fc153616`, not the pinned hash. Pinning to a divergent mirror means the Bible's rendered "truth" (including the still-retired `rapp-rappid/2.0` schema name) reads as if it were canonical.

2. **The four-leg model itself is stale.** DRIFT_TRIANGLE.md's own Check #1 requires `sha256(rapp-god/ecosystem-spec.json) == sha256(rapp-map/ecosystem-spec.json)`. This currently fails structurally: `kody-w/rapp-map/ecosystem-spec.json` no longer holds a spec mirror at all. Under the ratified RAPP1 migration (`kody-w/RAPP/RAPP1_AUTHORITY.json`, `RAPP1_STATUS.md`, `RAPP1_OWNER_ACTIONS.md`), it was deliberately replaced with a `registry-path-status`/`quarantined-candidate` refusal document (`"consumer_requirement": "REFUSE this document as an authenticated RAPP/1 registry"`) — confirmed as the *intended* state by rapp-map's own passing standing-guard self-check (`registry-quarantine: ecosystem-spec.json refused as authenticated registry`). DRIFT_TRIANGLE.md describes the pre-RAPP1 "two byte-identical grail mirrors" architecture as current fact, with no acknowledgment of the quarantine.

**Winning authority:** `kody-w/RAPP` CONSTITUTION Article LIII (sweep discipline) + Article LV (RAPP/1 rev-5 is the living protocol authority) + `RAPP1_AUTHORITY.json`/`RAPP1_STATUS.md`, which supersede the legacy ecosystem-spec.json byte-mirror model this page still documents as ground truth.

**Remediation:** re-pin from `kody-w/RAPP/specs/ecosystem-spec.json`'s canonical bytes (or, if rapp-god is to remain the intended pin source, first land the companion `rapp-god` fix so its bytes match canonical); update the four-leg description to reflect rapp-map's current registry-quarantine role instead of a byte-identical mirror, or point readers to `RAPP1_STATUS.md` for the live state.

**Not auto-fixed:** this run only files/comments; it does not edit canon, specs, or mirrors.

## Re-sweep 2026-09-28 (weekly Article LIII standing-guard) — correcting the 2026-09-07 "resolved" read; still open and real

Re-checked `DRIFT_TRIANGLE.md` on `main` from a fresh checkout. It has had **no commits since `7c89f12`** ("docs: retire stale ecosystem mirror claims", 2026-08-23) — the page's disposition table has not changed since that rewrite. The 2026-09-07 comment on this issue said the table "now matches the reconciled state" including "`kody-w/rapp-map/ecosystem-spec.json` (now a signed `rapp/1-registry`, registry_seq 2...)" — but that's not what the page text says. The current table still reads:

> `kody-w/rapp-map:ecosystem-spec.json` | 1,020-byte `quarantined-candidate` status document; not a mirror.

That was accurate as of the 2026-08-23 observation baked into the page. It is no longer accurate: `kody-w/rapp-map/ecosystem-spec.json` is now 5,381 bytes, schema `rapp/1-registry`, `registry_seq: 2` (published `2026-09-02T12:41:49Z`), and `rapp-map`'s own `RAPP1_STATUS.md` states plainly "`ecosystem-spec.json` is the estate's signed `rapp/1-registry`" — i.e. the opposite of "quarantined, not a mirror." `rapp-map`'s standing-guard self-check (re-run this sweep) confirms the signature verifies: `registry: ecosystem-spec.json verified: owner=rappid:@kody-w/estate-owner:b5814e45e998… seq=2 kinds=14`.

So the 2026-09-07 "resolved" verdict appears to have been reasoned from sweep-time knowledge of `rapp-map`'s live state rather than from the actual rendered page bytes, which were (and remain) frozen at the pre-registry-publication snapshot. This is the Article LIII.7 "frozen never silently means wrong" case: the Sept 2 registry publication is a major canon change that this page has not been swept for.

Page framing itself ("Status: historical," no live sha pin) is otherwise fine and not in question — only the specific factual claim about `rapp-map`'s current disposition is stale.

**Remediation (unchanged in substance from the original ask):** update the `kody-w/rapp-map:ecosystem-spec.json` row to reflect its current signed-registry role (or drop the specific byte/status claim and point readers to `RAPP1_STATUS.md` for live state, consistent with how the page already treats the rev-5 authority pin).

No canon, spec, or mirror bytes edited by this run — issue/comment only, per Article LIII.

issue.title: drift(spine-ratchet-regression): canon-drift gate FAILs — CONSTITUTION.md 22→23, specs/SPEC.md 5→7, unwaived
issue.body:
## Why

Weekly standing-guard sweep (Constitution Article LIII). `python3 tools/spine.py gate --ratchet` is this repo's own mechanical drift-regression gate (per `SPINE.md`: "fail only if it got WORSE"). It currently fails:

```
WORSE  CONSTITUTION.md                        23 version(s)  (was 22)
same   RAPP1_AUTHORITY.json                   3 version(s)
same   agents/basic_agent.py                  12 version(s)
same   rapp_brainstem/agents/basic_agent.py   2 version(s)
WORSE  specs/SPEC.md                          7 version(s)  (was 5)

FAIL: canon drift increased.
```

`spine/waivers.json` is empty — per Article LIII.2 ("waivers pin their canon") and the gate's own message ("Align the file, or record a waiver in spine/waivers.json with a reason and an expiry"), this is unexplained drift.

## What changed (diffed `spine/vertebrae/estate-2026-07-25.egg` against current `estate-map.json`, both mechanical `canon` blob-sha observations)

**CONSTITUTION.md:**
- New repos carrying their own copy, not previously observed: `rapp-ai`, `rapp-constitution`
- Hash changed since baseline: `kody-w/RAPP` (the canonical source itself — expected, tracks the repo's own amendments) and `kody-w/RAR` (changed to a hash that does **not** match RAPP's current CONSTITUTION.md — worth a look: did RAR's copy converge to current canon, or drift to something else?)

**specs/SPEC.md:**
- New repos carrying their own copy: `rapp-apex-dino`, `rapp-dino`, `rapp-open`
- No existing repo's hash changed.

## Severity

Low-medium — most of the regression is organic estate growth (new repos starting with their own snapshot before converging), which the ratchet design expects to be handled via waiver or convergence, not silence. The one item worth owner attention is `RAR`'s CONSTITUTION.md landing on a hash that differs from both its own baseline value and RAPP's current canonical text.

## Suggested fix

Either:
1. Converge the listed repos' copies to the current canonical `kody-w/RAPP` bytes, or
2. Record a waiver in `spine/waivers.json` for the accepted-on-purpose divergence (each with a reason and an expiry, per the file's own schema note), which ratchets the baseline back down.

Not filed as a per-repo issue since the affected repos aren't in this session's scope and the regression is a single mechanical signal owned by this repo's gate; the owner is best placed to decide convergence vs. waiver per repo.

---
Filed by the weekly RAPP estate standing-guard sweep (Constitution Article LIII). Per LIII.1, "fixed" is a re-sweep verdict — this issue stays open until the next sweep confirms resolution.
